The same paper says "The SNOLAB setup has been upgraded with additional detectors for another science run"; no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) dates that later run or says whether it is taking data now. The Fermilab MINOS-cavern operation (the open Fermilab interval above) is still reported as ongoing in an arXiv paper of 15 October 2026 (arXiv:2610.22418, 'a SENSEI sensor placed underground in the MINOS cavern at Fermilab').
intervals.quote: based on data taken from September 9, 2022 to April 10, 2023

name: SENSEI Skipper-CCD detector
notes: The device changed generations over the experiment's history (0.0947 g protoSENSEI in 2019 to a ~2 g Skipper-CCD from 2020); none of the sources consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives a single 'current' mass or pixel count for 2026.

placements.note: Placed at the existing campus-level site site:fermilab-main-campus, which is also used for the Fermilab MINOS near-detector hall (kind detector, precision 3000 m); no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives a more precise coordinate for this specific cavern.
placements.quote: a prototype Skipper-CCD placed in the MINOS cavern, ... at the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (FNAL)

active_mass.note: This is the protoSENSEI (2019) device's mass; the 2020 device was ~2 g (see notes). No mass figure for the current (2026) Fermilab detector is given in the papers consulted (checked 2026-10-25).
active_mass.quote: a total active mass (before masking) of 0.0947 gram

pixel_count.note: Computed as 4 × 624 × 362 = 903,552 from the quoted quadrant geometry; not stated as a single total in the source. Cross-check: the source gives an active area of 1.086 cm × 1.872 cm and 15 μm × 15 μm pixels (724 × 1248 pixels), and 0.0947 g total active mass at 1.0476 × 10⁻⁷ g per pixel (about 904,000 pixels).
pixel_count.quote: The four amplifiers allow the Skipper-CCD to be divided into four equal-sized quadrants, each consisting of 624 rows of 362 pixels.

summary.plain: A tiny silicon chip called a skipper CCD, sensitive enough to count single electrons, sitting in a shielded underground hall at Fermilab to catch the faint signal of a very light dark matter particle.
summary.technical: Skipper-CCD detector operated in the MINOS cavern at Fermilab; protoSENSEI (2018-2019) had 0.0947 g active mass across ~904,000 pixels in four amplifier quadrants, superseded by a ~2 g high-resistivity Skipper-CCD from 2020, with operations continuing as of the May 2026 spurious-charge paper (arXiv:2605.30281).

technology.quote: Skipper Charge-Coupled Devices (Skipper-CCDs) are a leading technology in the search for sub-GeV dark matter
technology.value: Skipper charge-coupled device (CCD): a high-resistivity silicon CCD with sub-electron readout noise, counting individual ionization electrons
